A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 13 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including figures, tables and appendices, are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, benchmark alignment scores, component ablations and a user study involving 61 participants.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, robustness experiments, non-contradictory prompt evaluation and failure analysis.

M1.justification: The method retains LLM-generated proxy prompts, concept substitution and injection at assigned denoising intervals. The decomposition instructions and in-context examples are retained. Naming the framework SAP, testing alternative models and adding diagnostic attention analysis do not establish a changed generation procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on simple, non-contradictory prompts through PartiPrompts-Simple (Table 6). Whoops!, Whoops-Hard and ContraBench remain the principal contradictory-prompt benchmarks. ContraBench retains the same 40 prompt scenarios despite reordering and minor wording differences.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds Annealing Guidance, VL-DNP, R2F on FLUX-schnell and a reimplementation of R2F on FLUX-dev. The original comparators remain. Annealing also joins the user study and qualitative comparisons, substantially expanding the methods evaluated against SAP.

E3.justification: v2 introduces controlled interval perturbations with fixed proxy texts and uniform windows of three or five steps. It also tests Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and specifies reuse of the same proxies and intervals for quantitative SD3 evaluation. The existing 50-step generation budget and GPT-4o alignment-scoring rubric remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends the original component and timing analyses with attention-map diagnostics, controlled interval perturbations, alternative-LLM evaluation, a non-contradictory-prompt check, and categorized failures with manual proxy correction (Figure 3, Tables 4–7, Figure 12). The qualitative multi-seed gallery is reduced from six prompt cases to three.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging alignment scores over three fixed random seeds per prompt. Neither introduces confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests. The additional robustness scores and failure-category percentages do not establish a changed uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The original Table 1 scores remain unchanged, including 85.10/62.13/66.16 for the FLUX-based method. However, Table 3 changes the two-proxy score from 50.73 to 60.26 without explaining the revision. v2 adds extensive baseline, SD3, perturbation and alternative-LLM results, plus PartiPrompts-Simple scores of 93.46 for FLUX and 93.06 for SAP.

T1.justification: The contextual-contradiction definition and mathematical description of proxy prompts and timestep intervals retain their meaning. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. The new contradiction diagram and attention-map discussion provide conceptual and empirical explanations rather than new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and central introduction/conclusion claims remain a training-free, LLM-assisted framework that resolves contextual contradictions through stage-aware proxy prompting and improves semantic alignment. SAP is a new name for the retained contribution; the additional experiments primarily strengthen its support.

C2.justification: v2 adds an attention-based account of competing token influences and distinguishes coarse-stage sensitivity from tolerance to exact timestep boundaries. Its failure analysis attributes most failures to proxy selection rather than interval assignment. The revised two-proxy discussion now describes performance as close to the full method, replacing v1's emphasis on substantial underperformance.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the previously omitted full Whoops-Hard prompt list, adds a project-page address, describes human filtering of ContraBench candidates and discusses embedding overhead. Figure 7 also specifies steps 1 and 14 where v1 only said 'too early' and 'too late'. These are documentation additions; the core instruction and evaluation templates remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to the GPT-4 technical report, Dynamic VLM-Guided Negative Prompting and Navigating with Annealing Guidance Scale in Diffusion Space. Related work now mentions annealed guidance, but the positioning around spurious correlations, semantic alignment, multi-prompt conditioning and LLM guidance remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: Beyond introducing SAP terminology, v2 extensively condenses and rewrites the coarse-to-fine explanation, decomposition discussion, experimental narrative and conclusion. It inserts a dedicated entanglement-analysis section, moves the realism discussion into supplementary material, and reorganizes the appendix into separately titled sections.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and extensively restructures displays. It adds contradiction and attention diagrams, rearranges the coarse-to-fine figure, expands comparison grids and tables, revises the SD3 display, and distributes supplementary examples across larger figures. Existing instruction tables are reformatted, alongside new robustness tables and the Whoops-Hard list.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support by testing timing sensitivity, LLM dependence and behavior on ordinary prompts, while expanding comparisons across diffusion backbones. Its failure analysis clarifies practical limitations, and publishing the Whoops-Hard list improves reproducibility. These additions address important gaps in v1's validation. The unexplained two-proxy score revision and continued absence of uncertainty estimates limit confidence, but do not outweigh the gains.
